actions.name: Epic Resistance
actions.value: Eldrick chooses one condition, spell, or other effect currently affecting him and rolls 1d20. On an 11+, the effect ends on him. Eldrick can use this action even if he would otherwise be unable to take actions, his actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters his game statistics.

fluffInfo.value: You learn the creature's Immunities, as well as its Air Form trait.

fluffInfo.name: (20+) An Octarine Storm
fluffInfo.value: You recognize its Chain Lightning, Meteor Strike, Quake, and Icy Bolt actions.

fluffInfo.name: (25+) Exceedingly Resilient
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Eldritch Cataclysms rule the skies, and never willingly descend to the ground. Instead, it rains down lightning, meteors, and icy blasts from above. The temperamental nature of these elementals means they delight in attacking with a variety of elements, and seldom use the same action two rounds in a row. They enjoy using their Meteor Strike on targets they've Frozen with Icy Bolt, and delight in using their Cyclonic Storm to blow away weapons and equipment dropped by targets of their Chain Lightning.

These enraged creatures revel in destruction but have little conception that anything could actually pose a threat to them. When confronted with a foe able to withstand their onslaught, they treat it as a personal affront, and furiously focus their subsequent attacks upon them occasionally to the exclusion of all else. Despite this single-minded strategy, an Eldritch Cataclysm can recognize when a creature is resistant or immune to its elemental attacks and tries to use only the most effective powers against its chosen target.

traits.name: Air Form
traits.value: The eldritch cataclysm can enter a Hostile creature's space and stop there. It can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.

traits.name: Cyclonic Storm
traits.value: The eldritch cataclysm emits a 120-foot Emanation of high winds that disperse gases and vapors and extinguish unprotected flames. Ranged attacks that pass through the area have Disadvantage. Objects that are not worn or carried are blown away 1d6 x 5 feet in a random direction. A creature that starts its turn in the Emanation is subjected to the following effect. *Strength Saving Throw:* DC 17 (flying creatures have Disadvantage). *Failure:* The target has the Slowed condition until the start of its next turn. Failure by 5 or More: The target is flung 1d6 x 5 feet in a random direction, landing with the Prone condition.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The eldritch cataclysm uses Chain Lighting or Icy Bolt, then uses Meteor Stike or Quake.

actions.name: Chain Lightning
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:* +12, range 120 ft. *Hit:* 21 (**3d8 + 7**) Lightning damage, the target has the Shocked condition until the end of the cataclysm's next turn, and the lightning leaps to another creature of the cataclysm's choice within 15 feet of the first target. The cataclysm makes a separate __Chain Lightning__ attack against the target. The cataclysm can make any number of __Chain Lightning__ attacks in this way, but a creature can be targeted only once each time the cataclysm takes this action.

actions.name: Icy Bolt
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:* +12, range 120 ft. *Hit:* 21 (**3d8 + 7**) Cold damage. *Hit or Miss:* The target and each creature within 5 feet of it are subjected to the following effect. *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 17. *Failure:* 18 (**4d8**) Cold damage, and the target has the Frozen condition (DC 17).

actions.name: Meteor Strike
actions.value: *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 17, each creature in a 15-foot radius, 40-foot tall Cylinder centered on a point the cataclysm can see within 120 feet. *Failure:* 18 (**4d8**) Fire damage plus 18 (**4d8**) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Quake
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 17, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the cataclysm. *Failure:* 28 (**8d6**) Thunder damage, and the target has the Prone condition. *Success* Half damage only.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Eldritch Crawlers weave together fractured timelines, and slip in and out of the Space Between Worlds with ease. They create their own Thin Places and travel through them back and forth as needed. When under attack, Eldritch Crawlers bend and alter the realities they exist in to shift to one where they are more likely to survive. They teleport around the battlefield and vanish into the Space Between Worlds as they need to, using Void Walker and their Fractured Reality Reaction, only to reemerge and attack their prey with Contaminated Venom.

traits.value: The troll regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns. If the troll takes Force or Psychic damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of the troll's next turn. The troll dies only if it starts its turn with 0 Hit Points and doesn't regenerate.

actions.name: Bite

bonusActions.value: The troll is so contaminated that it changes form constantly, growing new appendages or exploding out of its old skin into a new form. The troll may manifest one of the following mutations. The mutation stays in effect until a new one is chosen.

bonusActions.name: Grotesque Wings

bonusActions.name: Cyclopean Eye

traits.name: Central Nervous System

traits.name: Grappler

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (2/Day)

traits.name: Sensitive Gut

traits.name: Shapechanger
traits.value: The brain can use its action to polymorph into a different building or back into its true, tavern form. Its statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment or creatures it is wearing or carrying aren't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

traits.name: Warded

actions.name: Sling Mud

actions.name: Submerge
actions.value: If the bog body is in swampy terrain, they can submerge themself beneath the water and mud. While submerged, the bog body is heavily obscured.

If the bog body is grappling a target when they submerge, the target submerges with them. While submerged, the target is heavily obscured, restrained, and unable to breathe, and takes 4 (**1d8**) acid damage at the start of each of their turns.
A bog body can resurface as a bonus action. When they do so, a target they have grappled also resurfaces.

actions.name: Starcall (1/Day)

The creature chooses which side of the wall to end up on. The wall lasts for 1 minute or until the stag is incapacitated or dies. If possible, it tries to remain close to Burning targets to keep them on fire within its Enduring Flame aura.

Within the smoking ruins of Drakkenheim, Entropic Flames love to set buildings, furniture, and other objects on fire. They quickly turn the battlefield into a roiling inferno, one which cannot be extinguished easily thanks to their presence.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Entropic Watcher is a keen hunter who, by its very gaze, can cause a creature to grow weak and leave it open for annihilation. The Entropic Watcher focuses its gaze upon its prey and unleashes its eye beams towards it, knowing that if it can hold its gaze, the creature will succumb to the watcher's blasts much easier. It will use its Force Barrier and Shadow Crash to force its victims into an optimal position for it to strike, and grab them with its tendrils, holding them readily in its Withering Gaze.
If the Entropic Watcher is reduced to less than 50 Hit Points, it attempts to flee.

traits.name: Fully Contaminated
traits.value: The entropic watcher is immune to Contamination and has Advantage on saving throws against contaminated spells. The entropic watcher may cast contaminated spells even though it does not gain Contamination levels.

traits.name: Delerium Healing
traits.value: As an action, the entropic watcher can touch a delerium shard to regain 10 (3d6) Hit Points. Once the entropic watcher has used a delerium shard in this way, the shard can't be used in this manner again for 24 hours.

traits.name: Alien Intellect
traits.value: The entropic watcher is immune to any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts, as well as any divination spell that it refuses. Wisdom (*Insight*) checks made to ascertain the entropic watcher's intentions or sincerity have Disadvantage.

traits.name: Corrupting Aura
traits.value: A creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of the entropic watcher takes 14 (**4d6**) Necrotic damage.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The entropic watcher has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Withering Gaze
traits.value: The entropic watcher's eye creates a 150-foot long, 10-foot wide Line of withering magic. At the start of each of its turns, the entropic watcher decides which way the line faces and whether the line is active. Creatures in the Line have Vulnerability to Necrotic damage and can't regain Hit Points.

actions.name: The entropic watcher always takes its turn on Initiative count 20
actions.value: On its turn, the entropic watcher can use its movement and interaction as normal. However, it does not take an action or Bonus Action on its turn unless forced to do so by a spell or other effect. Instead, the entropic watcher takes one of the following Epic Actions at the end of each player character's turn:

entries: **Tendrils**: *Melee Attack Roll:* +10, reach 40 ft. *Hit:* 17 (**3d8 + 4**) Bludgeoning damage plus 9 (**2d8**) Necrotic damage, and if the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 18). While Grappled, the target has the Restrained condition. The entropic watcher has ten tendrils, each of which can grapple one creature.

**Insanity Beam (1/Round)**: *Ranged Attack Roll:* +10, range 60 ft. *Hit:* 22 (**4d10**) Necrotic damage, and the beam leaps to another target. The entropic watcher makes another Insanity Beam attack against a new target within 30 feet of the first. A creature can be targeted by only one Insanity Beam per turn. For each additional creature the beam hits, its damage increases by 5 (1d10).

actions.name: Dimensional Glide
actions.value: The entropic watcher moves up to its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attack action.

actions.name: Shadow Crash (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 18, each creature in a 30-foot radius Sphere centered on a point the entropic watcher can see within 150 feet. *Failure:* 36 (**8d8**) Necrotic damage. *Success* Half damage. *Failure or Success*: The Sphere's area is filled with magical Darkness for 1 minute or until the entropic watcher uses Shadow Crash again. A creature that ends its turn in the area takes 36 (**8d8**) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Contaminated Grasp
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 18, one creature Grappled by the entropic watcher. *Failure:* 16 (**3d10**) Necrotic damage, and the target gains one Contamination level. *Success* Half damage.

actions.name: Force Barrier
actions.value: The entropic watcher creates a shimmering octarine 10-foot-by-10-foot wall of force centered on a point within 150 feet. The wall lasts for 1 minute or until the entropic watcher has the Incapacitated condition or dies. The wall appears in any orientation it chooses, and can be free floating or resting on a solid surface. If the wall cuts through a creature's space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (the entropic watcher's choice).

Nothing can physically pass through the wall. It is immune to all damage and can't be dispelled by __Dispel Magic__. A __Disintegrate__ spell destroys the wall instantly, however. The wall also extends into the Ethereal Plane, blocking ethereal travel through the wall.

actions.name: Epic Resistance
actions.value: The entropic watcher chooses one condition, spell, or other effect currently affecting them and rolls 1d20. On an 11+, the effect ends on it. The entropic watcher can use this action even if it would otherwise be unable to take actions, its actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters its game statistics.

traits.value: The essence can enter an enemy's space and stop there, and they can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

traits.name: Gasping Aura

bonusActions.value: The essence imbues the power of breath in themself or another Elemental they can see within 30 feet of them, granting one of the following effects of that Elemental's choice:

entries: **Hide in Breath.** The Elemental tries to hide inside the body of a creature within 10 feet of them who isn't a Construct, an Elemental, an Ooze, or an Undead. While inside the target, the Elemental can't take actions and has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the target.

**Toxic Breath.** The Elemental exudes a noxious aura 10 feet in every direction for 1 minute or until dispersed by a moderate or stronger wind. That area is lightly obscured, and each creature who needs to breathe who starts their turn in that area must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned until the end of their next turn.

fluffInfo.name: (5+) Unstoppable Machine

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Executioner is not a foe to be defeated, but rather an obstacle to be avoided or a danger to escape. It is a reminder of the callous and uncontrollable dangers present in Drakkenheim. The Executioner's combat tactics vary based on whether it detects low-level characters trespassing in Slaughterstone Square or high-level characters trying to defeat the machine itself. The Executioner pursues its targets within Slaughterstone Square, but never leaves the plaza.

When the Executioner detects creatures trespassing on Slaughterstone Square, it responds first by using Summon Grasping Shadows, followed up by Death Grip to try to prevent their escape. Meanwhile, it uses Lumber Forward to gain ground. You should embrace clever solutions that characters invent to escape or bypass the Executioner. As long as your players aren't trying to destroy it, the Executioner will only use Guillotine Blade against a Restrained target within its melee range, and does not make ranged attacks nor activate its Necrotic Vents aura.

However, should your players engage the Executioner directly in combat, do not pull any punches. They have made an incredibly foolish mistake by confronting a well-telegraphed deathtrap and should be served their just desserts. It activates its Necrotic Vents, and then relentlessly attacks with its Guillotine Blade. The Executioner throws the massive weapon to hit targets trying to avoid it in melee, or those that try to harm it with ranged weapons or spells. If it encounters any impediment in its way (such as a __Wall of Force__), it crushes it with Destroyer.

fluffInfo.value: *I admire their divine focus but it's the controlling you with ghosts thing where they lose me.*

An Exorcist comes prepared to deal with evil entities, sinister spirits, and fearsome fiends. Equipped with their holy symbol, a book of prayers, and a bag of ritualistic baubles, Exorcists stand ready to face the most unnatural and otherworldly entities of the realms. Some Exorcists, however, are so familiar with the ways of the undead, they can summon spirits into hosts. In some rare cases, Exorcists allow demons to inhabit the living.

fluffInfo.name: Exorcists Minions
fluffInfo.value: Exorcists deal with all manner of entities. They can call forth Specters, Ghosts, Demons, Wraiths, and other extraplanar entities. The most horrifying creation of the Exorcist is the Soulbound Host, which occurs when an Exorcist allows themself to be a vessel for demonic, extraplanar, or fairy entities, attempting to harness the power of such beings. Most are driven mad during the process.

entries: **Personality Trait:** I speak to the dead often, sometimes when I am not even sure if they are there..
**Bond:** The understanding of life and death grants us power over the planes that few have dared to grasp.
**Ideal:** It is in control of demons and ghosts that we will transcend to our true potential.
**Flaw:** I am sure I have the strength within me to host a demon or spirit without succumbing to its will.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe
fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *Medicine* or *Religion* gain Advantage on Wisdom (*Insight*) or Intelligence (*Investigation*) checks to study an Exorcist, learning the following based on the result:

fluffInfo.name: (5+) Demons and Undead
fluffInfo.value: You recognize the Exorcist's Immunities as well as their Expel Evil action.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Master of Possession
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of the Exorcist's Grasping Ghost action.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Weak of Character and Body
fluffInfo.value: You learn the Exorcist's Strength and Charisma ability scores and saving throws.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Exorcist relies on its divine weapons and direct combat skills. They often reside in locations that have natural hazards where they can use their Grasping Ghosts to force enemies into danger. Hazards could include burning braziers, spiked pits, or a pool of blessed acid. If any foe has a summoned creature, the Exorcist dispatches it using Expel Evil, and destroy any undead foes with Last Rites.
If the Exorcist is in a losing situation, they attempt to use Spiritual Healing on themself before fleeing.

traits.name: Blessed Weapons
traits.value: When the Exorcist hits with any weapon, the weapon unleashes holy fire, causing the target to have the Burning condition (4d6 Radiant; included in the attacks below).

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The exorcist makes two attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Grasping Ghost.

actions.name: Radiant Sword
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +7, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 11 (**2d6 + 4**) Slashing damage, and the target has the Burning condition (4d6 Radiant).

actions.name: Blessed Crossbow
actions.value: *Ranged Attack Roll:* +7, range 80/320 ft. *Hit:* 9 (**1d10 + 4**) Piercing damage, and the target has the Burning condition (4d6 Radiant).

actions.name: Grasping Ghost
actions.value: *Strength Saving Throw:* DC 15, one creature the exorcist can see within 60 feet. *Failure:* 18 (**4d8**) Necrotic damage, and the target is moved 30 feet in a horizontal direction of the exorcist's choice. At the end of this movement, the target has the Immobilized condition until the end of the exorcist's next turn. *Success* Half damage only.

actions.name: Expel Evil (1/Day)
actions.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 15, each Celestial, Fey, Fiend, and Undead that can see and hear the exorcist. *Failure:* The target has the Frightened and Incapacitated conditions and must move as far from the exorcist as it can on its turns. The effect lasts for 1 minute or until the target takes damage, the exorcist has the Incapacitated condition, or the exorcist dies.

actions.name: Last Rites (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 15, one creature the exorcist can see within 60 feet that isn't a Celestial or Construct (Fiends and Undead have Disadvantage). *Failure:* 36 (**8d8**) Radiant damage. If the target is a Fiend or Undead, it instead takes 64 Radiant damage and is turned to ash if the effect reduces it to 0 Hit Points. *Success* Half damage.

bonusActions.name: Spiritual Healing
bonusActions.value: One creature the exorcist can see regains 35 10d6 Hit Points. Once a creature benefits from Spiritual Healing, it can't do so again until it finishes a Short or Long Rest.

fluffInfo.value: A Soulbound Host is the physical body of an apothecary who has willingly allowed an extraplanar creature to possess them, trapping the powerful outsider in a mortal form. Powerful yet vulnerable, Soulbound Hosts loathe their creators. They wander the world for the means to reverse the curse of mortality placed upon them and return to their otherworldly domains.

Exorcist and Alienist apothecaries do not primarily study the body, and rarely practice the type of magic and science which leads to mutant horrors and flesh-stitched abominations. They are instead concerned with the supernatural forces of the mind and soul. Many research and contact powerful extraplanar entities, eager to possess mortals as a means of entering the material world. These apothecaries learn how to create Soulbound Hosts as a powerful means to contain and fight back against these dangerous otherworldly foes.

fluffInfo.name: Desperate Gambit
fluffInfo.value: A Soulbound Host is usually created under truly desperate circumstances, such as when a heroic apothecary faces a dangerous otherworldly being such as a demon, fey, spirit, or inscrutable entity from the Space Between Worlds. Not only are these planar invaders pernicious foes, many are effectively immortal—often these creatures simply reform when killed outside their native planes. Thus, an apothecary who lacks the ability to defeat the demon on their own, or who wishes to defeat a powerful outsider in a more permanent fashion, may instead decide upon a heroic act of self-sacrifice by turning themselves into a Soulbound Host.

fluffInfo.name: Preparing the Trap
fluffInfo.value: Using an array of implanted metals, ingested tinctures, mental preparations, and occult incantations, a skilled apothecary may willingly prepare their body for possession. During the process, the apothecary can weave a unique spiritual trap. It then falls to the apothecary to convince the otherworldly creature to possess them, an act that many outsiders are eager to do. Thus, the canny apothecary preys on the ego of the monster itself.

fluffInfo.name: Mortal Curse
fluffInfo.value: When the outsider inhabits the body, the apothecary's soul departs, leaving the extraplanar creature to take their place spiritually. If this mortal form is killed or destroyed, the bound creature does not simply return to their plane of origin. Instead, the spirit departs to the afterworlds like any other mortal soul, losing their accumulated otherworldly power forever. Thus, the Soulbound Host becomes both a prison and a death sentence for the other wielding being tricked into the apothecary's body.

fluffInfo.name: Rogue Hosts
fluffInfo.value: Unfortunately, this act of self-sacrifice is not without its imperfections. The apothecary's body is filled with otherworldly essence, and while the creature's power is greatly diminished, they often remain extremely dangerous—allies of the departed apothecary may still find it challenging to slay the Soulbound Host. Many escape, wandering the world with stolen lives and even assuming the identity of their host while they search for the means to escape their now mortal form. All bound outsiders are painfully aware of their new mortality, frustrated that returning to their planes of origin is not a simple matter of destroying their flesh-cage or switching their essence into a different host, one which lacks the binding wards placed by the apothecary.

fluffInfo.name: Price of Freedom
fluffInfo.value: Trapped outsiders can win their freedom by calling back the soul of the apothecary who trapped them, and resurrecting them into their body. This is a thing many outsiders are loathe to do out of fiendish ego, since it puts the original soul in a bargaining position. In this way, the apothecary can force the spirit to accept a bargain which requires them to remain in their own worlds for at least the duration of the apothecary's lifetime.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Extraplanar Magic

fluffInfo.name: (20+) Cursed Fate
fluffInfo.value: You recognize its desperation caused by its spirit-bound mortality and its Reactions.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: A Soulbound Host is a careful combatant. Though powerful, the last thing they want is to be killed in their mortal form. If they are seriously injured, they often attempt to bargain, offering power and knowledge to assailants who spare them.

fluffInfo.value: When a will-o'-wisp basks in the eternal sunset of the Plane of Fey, a change overcomes the malevolent spirit that lies at its heart. In place of a wisps' despair, a faerie develops a guileful and mischievous cunning.

These faeries often pair themselves with more powerful creatures, such as a fey queen with a penchant for collecting waifs and strays, or a territorial suneater owlbear. They act as a lure for such a creatures, coaxing unwary wanderers to follow their cheerful nimbus. If all goes according to the faerie's plan, both faerie and host will gain a meal from this symbiotic mutualism.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Far Dweller Abductors are not fighters, and simply wish to gather specimens and study them. When Abductors appear, they usually do so when a creature is resting or asleep. They rely on their Unfathomable Presence to confuse and dismantle their target. They use use Mind Warp or Devour Thoughts to weaken the mind of their target before attempting to Abduct them.

The Far Dweller Abductors do not wish to be observed or remembered, and do not want even their dead left behind to be discovered and known to the creatures they are researching. A Far Dweller Abductor will teleport away and use __Plane Shift__ if it has lost the upper hand, is outnumbered, or feels in any way threatened. If a Far Dweller Abductor dies, any Far Dwellers still engaged in battle attempt to take their bodies and vanish as quickly as possible, attempting to leave no trace of their presence.

fluffInfo.value: A Soulbound Host is the physical body of an apothecary who has willingly allowed an extraplanar creature to possess them, trapping the powerful outsider in a mortal form. Powerful yet vulnerable, Soulbound Hosts loathe their creators. They wander the world for the means to reverse the curse of mortality placed upon them and return to their otherworldly domains.

Exorcist and Alienist apothecaries do not primarily study the body, and rarely practice the type of magic and science which leads to mutant horrors and flesh-stitched abominations. They are instead concerned with the supernatural forces of the mind and soul. Many research and contact powerful extraplanar entities, eager to possess mortals as a means of entering the material world. These apothecaries learn how to create Soulbound Hosts as a powerful means to contain and fight back against these dangerous otherworldly foes.

fluffInfo.name: Desperate Gambit
fluffInfo.value: A Soulbound Host is usually created under truly desperate circumstances, such as when a heroic apothecary faces a dangerous otherworldly being such as a demon, fey, spirit, or inscrutable entity from the Space Between Worlds. Not only are these planar invaders pernicious foes, many are effectively immortal—often these creatures simply reform when killed outside their native planes. Thus, an apothecary who lacks the ability to defeat the demon on their own, or who wishes to defeat a powerful outsider in a more permanent fashion, may instead decide upon a heroic act of self-sacrifice by turning themselves into a Soulbound Host.

fluffInfo.name: Preparing the Trap
fluffInfo.value: Using an array of implanted metals, ingested tinctures, mental preparations, and occult incantations, a skilled apothecary may willingly prepare their body for possession. During the process, the apothecary can weave a unique spiritual trap. It then falls to the apothecary to convince the otherworldly creature to possess them, an act that many outsiders are eager to do. Thus, the canny apothecary preys on the ego of the monster itself.

fluffInfo.name: Mortal Curse
fluffInfo.value: When the outsider inhabits the body, the apothecary's soul departs, leaving the extraplanar creature to take their place spiritually. If this mortal form is killed or destroyed, the bound creature does not simply return to their plane of origin. Instead, the spirit departs to the afterworlds like any other mortal soul, losing their accumulated otherworldly power forever. Thus, the Soulbound Host becomes both a prison and a death sentence for the other wielding being tricked into the apothecary's body.

fluffInfo.name: Rogue Hosts
fluffInfo.value: Unfortunately, this act of self-sacrifice is not without its imperfections. The apothecary's body is filled with otherworldly essence, and while the creature's power is greatly diminished, they often remain extremely dangerous—allies of the departed apothecary may still find it challenging to slay the Soulbound Host. Many escape, wandering the world with stolen lives and even assuming the identity of their host while they search for the means to escape their now mortal form. All bound outsiders are painfully aware of their new mortality, frustrated that returning to their planes of origin is not a simple matter of destroying their flesh-cage or switching their essence into a different host, one which lacks the binding wards placed by the apothecary.

fluffInfo.value: *When encountering a Fractal Lepidoptera, characters can get stranded in the Border Ethereal Plane. This has the potential to derail a campaign. Here are a few suggestions on how to run this scenario instead:*

entries: When the lepidoptera dies, the fabric of reality temporarily weakens and everyone can safely return to the Prime Material Plane.

Immediately after the lepidoptera dies, the party needs to succeed in a skill challenge to traverse the veil between the planes. Each character can contribute to the skill challenge by suggesting actions that they take to help find the veil, withstand the pull of the Ethereal Plane, and open a gate.
The group succeeds if they make 4 successful DC 15 skill checks before 3 failures.
The characters must harvest the animus of the lepidoptera and craft a fractal key.

fluffInfo.name: Lair effect
fluffInfo.value: Fractal Lepidoptera transform reality around them, manifesting the following effect:

fluffInfo.name: Quantum Entanglement
fluffInfo.value: Creatures taking a Long Rest within 1 mile of the lepidoptera must succeed on a DC 17 Charisma saving throw or gain a pattern effect. Creatures can repeat the saving throw at the end of each Long Rest once they are outside the range of Quantum Entanglement. Casting __Lesser Restoration__ or similar spells of higher level on an affected creature can remove the pattern effect.

table.title: Fractal Lepidoptera Patterns
rows: Something unseen hampers you. You gain the Staggered condition.
On each of your turns, you can only walk in straight lines in the direction of either north, south, east, or west.
Your hands start to flutter uncontrollably. You gain the Clumsy condition.
You can only speak in haikus, rhyming couplets, or iambic pentameter.
You float an inch above the ground. Your walking Speed is unchanged and Difficult Terrain does not affect you.
You gain the ability to see polarized light and the ultraviolet spectrum. You see invisible objects and creatures, and you can see into the Ethereal Plane.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe
fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *Nature* gain Advantage on Intelligence (*Arcana*) checks when they take the Study action to examine a lepidoptera, learning the following based on the result.

fluffInfo.name: (5+) Mothlike Features
fluffInfo.value: You recognize its Phototaxis trait.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Chaotic Patterns
fluffInfo.value: You learn the lepidoptera's Quantum Entanglement and Tessellation features.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Multidimensional
fluffInfo.value: You know of the creature's Multidimensional Presence and Incomprehensible Vision features.

fluffInfo.name: (20+) Creature of Energy
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of its Vulnerabilities and Energy Form trait.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The lepidoptera flies through creatures while making Fractal Wing attacks, scattering foes with its Energy Form trait. If at least one enemy is Staggered, it targets them with Tessellation. The lepidoptera uses Criss Cross to protect itself from attacks on the border Ethereal Plane.

fluffInfo.name: Animus:
fluffInfo.value: Elemental.

fluffInfo.name: Dust:
fluffInfo.value: Elemental Dust.

traits.name: Fully Contaminated
traits.value: The lepidoptera is immune to Contamination and has Advantage on saving throws against contaminated spells. The lepidoptera may cast contaminated spells even though it does not gain Contamination levels.

traits.name: Delerium Healing
traits.value: As an action, the lepidoptera can touch a delerium shard to regain 10 (3d6) Hit Points. Once the lepidoptera has used a delerium shard in this way, the shard can't be used in this manner again for 24 hours.

traits.name: Alien Intellect
traits.value: The lepidoptera is immune to any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts, as well as any divination spell that it refuses. Wisdom (*Insight*) checks made to ascertain the lepidoptera's intentions or sincerity have Disadvantage.

traits.name: Energy Form
traits.value: The lepidoptera can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement to do so, and it can enter a creature's space and stop there. The first time it enters a creature's space on a turn, that creature is moved 20 feet in a random direction.

traits.name: Incomprehensible Vision
traits.value: A creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of the lepidoptera and can see it is subjected to the following effect. *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 13. *Failure:* The target has the Staggered condition until the start of its next turn. *Success* The target is transported to the Border Ethereal. If the target is already on the Border Ethereal, they are transported to the Material Plane instead.

Unless *surprised*, a creature can avert their eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of their turn. If the creature does so, it can't see the lepidoptera until the start of its next turn. fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Garmyr warriors fight as a pack, following their leader on the hunt. They choose the juiciest, most delicious-looking target as their prey, favoring unarmored or feeble-looking creatures. Garmyr group up and focus their attacks until they bring down their target, unless a more dangerous threat prompts them to respond.

Garmyr crave blood and close-quarters battle, closing the distance to attack with their bites even when it may be more advantageous for them to keep their distance using their spears. Garmyr don't stop attacking a foe once they've downed them—they start feasting instead. Garmyr make Bite attacks against downed foes in the midst of battle, making Unconscious and dying characters especially vulnerable to the Garmyr's appetites.

Garymr are mostly heedless in battle unless their numbers are significantly cut down. Although they prefer to start battles when they outnumber their enemies, they flee as the fight turns against them. However, Garmyr might also attempt to flee once they've secured a meal—a group of Garmyr who manage to down one character in a group might decide to scoop up the victim and enjoy their meal elsewhere rather than continuing to fight.

The ratling will Enrage and start hurling other ratlings at its enemy as it charges forward, bearing down on the creature with claws and teeth. These brutes are relentless in their attacks, and generally much braver—or dumber—than other ratlings. They are unlikely to flee from harm.
If the rest of the ratlings begin to flee, the Giant Ratling will follow, but it will usually be the last to turn tail as it enjoys pummeling and gnawing on flesh a bit too much.

traits.name: Immutable Form
traits.value: The gibbering mouther is immune to any power, spell, or effect that would alter their form.

traits.name: Primordial Influence
traits.value: A dazed enemy who starts their turn within 20 feet of the gibbering mouther must make a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, that creature's body is altered in an otherworldly way of the GM's choice—they might flicker in and out of reality, sprout miniature fingers from their fingers, or have their physical form altered in a similarly alien way. This alteration doesn't affect the creature's game statistics. A cure ailment power of 4th order or higher, a __greater restoration__ spell, or a similar supernatural effect reverses this alteration.

While altered in this way, a creature must repeat the saving throw whenever they finish a long rest. On a failed save, their previous alteration worsens or they experience another chaotic alteration of the GM's choice. If a creature fails this saving throw three times after their initial alteration, they transform into a gibbering mouther controlled by the GM, and only a __wish__ spell can restore the creature to their original form.

traits.name: Phantasmal Cone
traits.value: The dreamholder's central eye creates an area of phantasmagoric horrors—illusory manifestations unique to each creature—within a 150-foot cone. At the start of each of its turns, the dreamholder decides which way the cone faces and whether the cone is active. Each creature within the cone at the end of the dreamholder's turn must succeed on a DC 20 Intelligence saving throw or take 22 (**4d10**) psychic damage and become frightened of the dreamholder and the illusions within the area until the end of the dreamholder's next turn.
As an affected creature is surrounded by these illusions, the source of its fear is in every direction, rendering it unable to move in any direction while it can see these sources of its fear.

traits.name: Inconsistent Incoporeality
traits.value: When the dreamholder takes 15 or more psychic or thunder damage in a single instance, it becomes corporeal until the start of its next turn. While corporeal, it loses its Incorporeal Movement trait; its immunity to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage; and its immunity to the grappled and restrained conditions.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.value: The dreamholder can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (**1d10**) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.value: If the dreamholder fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

actions.name: Dreameater
actions.value: *Melee Spell Attack:* +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. *Hit:* 49 (**8d10 + 5**) psychic damage.

actions.name: Eye Rays
actions.value: The dreamholder shoots five of the following magical eye rays at random (roll a d6 to determine which ray isn't fired), choosing one to five creatures it can see within 120 feet of it:

entries: **1. Charm Ray**: The target must succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by the dreamholder for 1 hour, or until the dreamholder harms the target.
**2. Confusion Ray**: The target must succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw or be afflicted by the confusion spell until the end of its next turn.

**3. Static Ray**: The target must make a DC 20 Intelligence saving throw, taking 21 (**6d6**) psychic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. On a failed save, a target has muddled thoughts for 1 minute. During that time, it rolls a d6 and subtracts the number rolled from all its attack rolls and ability checks, as well as its Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

**4. Rot Ray**: The target must make a DC 20 Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, its grey matter deteriorates, it takes 28 (**8d6**) necrotic damage, and it has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls it makes until the end of its next turn. On a success it takes half as much damage and suffers no additional effects.

**5. Incorporeal Shunt Ray**: The target must succeed on a DC 20 Charisma saving throw or become momentarily incorporeal, be pushed up to 30 feet directly away from the dreamholder, and then rematerialise. The creature takes 36 (**8d8**) force damage if it rematerialises inside an object. If the creature rematerialises in another creature's space, both creatures take this damage. The target is then pushed to the nearest unoccupied space.

**6. Nightmare Ray**: The target is assailed by illusory manifestations of its fears. It must make a DC 20 Intelligence saving throw, taking 44 (**8d10**) psychic damage on a failure or half as much damage on a success.

fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *Arcana* or *History* gain Advantage on Intelligence (*Arcana*) checks when they take the Study action to examine a Graffiti, learning the following based on their result:

fluffInfo.name: (5+) Reforming Words
fluffInfo.value: You learn of the creature's Regeneration ability.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Manifesting Visions
fluffInfo.value: You recognize the creature's Summon Public Opinion and Transposition abilities.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Magical Erasure
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of the creature's Solvent Susceptibility and Antimagic Susceptibility traits.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: When a creature draws a Graffiti's attention, it uses illusions to confuse its targets. It then uses Summon Public Opinion and watches the drama unfold. To keep things interesting, the Graffiti uses its Transposition ability to see how creatures respond to situations when they're forced to approach them from new perspectives.

When the graffiti is in the heart of the action, it targets the most influential creature with Satire. Should the graffiti decide its target is sufficiently entertaining, or dangerous, it will flee the situation. If the graffiti is reduced to 0 Hit Points, it plays dead and then escapes at the first opportunity.

traits.name: Antimagic Susceptibility
traits.value: The graffiti is incapacitated while in the area of antimagic. If targeted by __Dispel Magic__, the graffiti must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against the caster's spell save DC or become Unconscious for 1 minute.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.value: The graffiti regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns. If the graffiti is splashed with water, targeted by __Prestidigitation__, or takes Cold damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of its next turn. Its body is destroyed only if it starts its turn with 0 Hit Points and doesn't regenerate.

traits.name: Solvent Susceptibility
traits.value: The graffiti is instantly destroyed by Universal Solvent.

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.value: The graffiti can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

traits.name: Surface Bound
traits.value: The graffiti can only move along contiguous flat surfaces, such as walls or floors.

actions.name: Satire
actions.value: The graffiti shapes itself into a satirical representation of a foe. *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 15, one creature within 60 feet that can see the graffiti. *Failure:* 10 (**3d6**) Psychic damage and the target has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the start of the graffiti's next turn. *Success* Half damage only.

actions.name: Transposition
actions.value: The air quivers around creatures near the graffiti. *Charisma Saving Throw:* DC 15, up to five creatures the graffiti can see within 120 feet. *Failure:* The creature teleports to an unoccupied space capable of supporting the creature within 120 feet.

actions.name: Summon Public Opinion (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The graffiti conjures a swarm of Drakkenheim citizen spirits within 120 feet of itself. The swarm uses the Chorus stat block. The chorus acts immediately after the graffiti on the same Initiative count, and it obeys the graffiti. The chorus disappears after 1 minute or the graffiti dies

entries: **Resistances**: bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from mundane attacks that aren't adamantine

traits.name: False Appearance
traits.value: While motionless, the giant is indistinguishable from a statue.

traits.name: Stone Flesh
traits.value: When a creature attacks the giant with a melee weapon that isn't adamantine and rolls a 1 on the d20 for that attack, that weapon is destroyed if it is mundane. If that weapon is supernatural, it loses all supernatural properties for 1 hour.

actions.name: Greatclub
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 19 (**3d8 + 6**) bludgeoning damage. If the same creature is hit twice with this attack on a turn, they have disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of their next turn.

actions.name: Rock
actions.value: *Ranged Weapon Attack:* +9 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. *Hit:* 28 (**4d10 + 6**) bludgeoning damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 17 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

traits.value: The gravekeeper sheds Bright Light in a 60-foot radius. A creature that starts its turn in the Bright Light takes 10 (**3d6**) Radiant damage.

actions.name: The gravekeeper always takes its turn on Initiative count 20
actions.value: On its turn, the gravekeeper can use its movement and interaction as normal. However, it does not take an action or Bonus Action on its turn unless forced to do so by a spell or other effect. Instead, the gravekeeper takes one of the following Epic Actions at the end of each player character's turn:

actions.name: Slam
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +9, reach 10 ft. *Hit:* 22 (**4d8 + 4**) Bludgeoning damage plus 10 (**3d6**) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Lantern Blast
actions.value: Magical octarine beams flash from one of the Gravekeeper's many lanterns at one creature it can see within 120 feet that is not behind Total Cover, subjecting it to one of the following effects (the gravekeeper can only use each blast once per round):

entries: **Dispelling Blast**: *Intelligence Saving Throw:* DC 18. *Failure:* 35 (**10d6**) Psychic damage. Any spell or magical effect on the target ends, and it has the Bewildered condition (save ends). *Success* Half damage only.

**Forceful Blast**: *Strength Saving Throw:* DC 18. *Failure:* 35 (**10d6**) Force damage, and the target is pushed 20 feet away from the gravekeeper and has the Prone condition. *Success* Half damage only.
**Blinding Blast**: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 18. *Failure:* 35 (**10d6**) Radiant damage, and the target has the Blinded condition (save ends). *Success* Half damage only.
**Contaminating Blast**: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 18. *Failure:* 35 (**10d6**) Necrotic damage, and the target gains one Contamination level. *Success* Half damage only.
**Igniting Blast**: *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 18. *Failure:* 35 (**10d6**) Fire damage, and the target has the Burning condition (10d6 Fire). *Success* Half damage only.
**Freezing Blast**: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 18. *Failure:* 35 (**10d6**) Cold damage, and the target has the Frozen condition (DC 18). *Success* Half damage only.

actions.name: Glide (1/Round)
actions.value: The gravekeeper moves up to its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attack action.

actions.name: Sludge Column (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 18, each creature in a 10-foot radius, 60-foot tall Cylinder, centered on a point within 120 feet of the Gravekeeper. *Failure:* 42 (**12d6**) Necrotic damage, and the target gains one Contamination level. *Success* Half damage only.

actions.name: Animate Walls (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 18, each creature within 10 feet of any number of walls within 120 feet of the gravekeeper. *Failure:* The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 18). The wall sprouts limbs to facilitate this grapple, which disappear when the condition ends.

actions.name: Epic Resistance
actions.value: The gravekeeper chooses one condition, spell, or other effect currently affecting it and rolls 1d20. On an 11+, the effect ends on it. The gravekeeper can use this Epic Action even if it would otherwise be unable to take actions, its actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters its game statistics.

fluffInfo.value: Guardians of flourishing alpine forests, great fir drakes live peacefully among their saplings. Each day, the iridescent drakes use powerful magic to replenish their forest's soil and promote the growth of their beloved fir trees. Over the centuries, villagers and townsfolk have learned to live in peace with these largely benevolent beings.

People who live near a great fir drake's lair can visit its forest home and leave the drake small shiny tokens under trees they wish to cut down. If the people return the next day to find the tokens have been gathered and taken, they know the great fir drake has given its blessing for those tree to be felled. In thanks, villagers decorate the trees with lights to resemble the drake. Those who fail to leave an offering for the drake's hoard and cut down its fir trees enrage the legendary creature, and should prepare to face its thrashing, needle-covered tail.

traits.name: Illumination
traits.value: As a Bonus Action, the drake can produce dim light in a 15 ft radius, or bright light in a 15 ft radius and dim light for an additional 15 ft radius. The drake can end this effect as a Bonus Action.

traits.name: Prickly Pines

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)

actions.name: Multiattack

actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +9, reach 10 ft. *Hit:* 13 (**2d8 + 4**) Slashing damage plus 7 (**2d6**) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Incandescent Breath (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 19, each creature in a 90 ft long, 5 ft wide Line. *Failure:* 55 (**10d10**) Radiant damage. *Success* Half damage.

traits.name: Sticky Mucus
traits.value: When a creature hits the chrysalis with a melee attack, it must succeed on a DC 20 Strength saving throw or become disarmed as its weapon stays stuck to the creature. A creature can use an action to make a DC 20 Strength (*Athletics*) check, freeing a stuck weapon within its reach on a success. If the attack requires that the attacker touch the aboleth (GM's discretion), then the attacker becomes grappled (escape DC 20) on a failed save. While it is grappled, it can't use that limb. If the attack is a bite, then the creature can't speak while it is grappled in this way.

traits.name: Transitional State
traits.value: The chrysalis turns into an aboleth broodmother at the start of its fourth turn after becoming a chrysalis, ending any grapples it is a part of.

actions.name: Multiattack

A creature whose speed is reduced to 0 feet by this effect is restrained (escape DC 20).

actions.name: Granny Says
actions.value: The hag affects one other willing creature they can see within 30 feet of them with one of the following effects:

entries: The target magically switches places with the hag.
The target uses their reaction, if available, to make an attack.

actions.name: Naughty Mousey (3/Day; 5th-Level Spell; Concentration)
actions.value: The hag chooses a creature they can see within 60 feet of them and attempts to transform them into a Beast of the hag's choice with a challenge rating of 2 or lower. The target must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or be transformed for 1 minute (save ends at end of turn). While transformed, the target's game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the chosen Beast, though they retain their alignment, personality, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. The target's gear melds into the new form. They can't activate, use, wield, or otherwise benefit from any of their equipment. They can't speak or cast spells but can take any action the Beast can take. If the target drops to 0 hit points while in this form, they revert back to their original form with half the number of hit points they had before they transformed.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Grim Custodian does everything in their power to avoid combat, liberally using __Suggestion__ and __Detect Thoughts__. When directly confronted and with no one to protect them, they cast __Invisibility__ on themselves and flee. They focus on hiding their undead nature. Grim Custodians can use __Nystul's Magic Aura__ and __nondetection__ to foil divinations which would otherwise detect them, and __Major Image__ and Seeming to further disguise the truth.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Grotesque Gargantuans are violently territorial creatures. Unlike the randomly mutated creatures found throughout the Haze, these hideous entities are more in tune with the arcane elements of Drakkenheim. Their form appears more intentional, as does their purpose, though the truth behind this intention remains a mystery

Gargantuans often drag chunks of delerium along with them, and their massive arms can swing or throw them with ease. They place the stones in odd formations around the city and, if witnessed by another creature who isn't a Dreg or a Haze Hulk, they will violently lash out and chase the observerer down. The Gargantuan hurls huge boulders of delerium at them. Whatever their intention is, they will not abandon their territory, or their work, and rarely flee from the site they are working in.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Gutbuster is a massive, bloated hulk that constantly grows fleshy masses within its ever expanding belly. If left unchecked, a Gutbuster Hulk can grow to proportions so large that it crushes itself under its own weight. Ratlings love when this happens—it supplies them with food for weeks.

The Gutbuster maintains its form by ripping chunks of flesh from its body, hurling them at enemies. This contaminated flesh erupts in a shower of gore and necrotic fluids. A Gutbuster usually opens with this attack to ward off foes, and then waits for more flesh to grow to hurl it again. If its enemies close in around it, it uses its Bile Blast to coat the creatures in acid, or will Slam them with its massive fists.
The Gutbuster is slower moving than other Haze Hulks and rarely runs from a fight.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Gutwretch Dreg keeps its distance from other combatants, watching all creatures who dare approach while swinging its flail over its head. It often protects other Dregs, standing watch over them while they eat or tend to other matters.

The Dreg uses its Reactive trait, as well as its Flailing Guts Reaction to knock creatures out of its way the moment they come near. It will always try to move away from direct combat, preferring to keep its enemies at arm's length so it can continue to pummel them with its Gut Flail.
The Gutwretch Dreg will fight to protect its fellow Dregs and is often the last one to flee from combat.

entries: He has a flying speed of 60 feet.
He has resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from mundane attacks.
He has advantage on Dexterity (*Stealth*) checks and can attempt to hide without cover.

actions.value: While in this form, Harlo can't pick up or wield objects except for his Amethyst Die.

actions.name: Alluring Song
actions.value: The harpy starts singing a beautiful song. They continue singing until they choose to stop (no action required) or until they become deafened or incapacitated. When a non-harpy creature starts their turn within 200 feet of the singing harpy, if that creature shares a language with the harpy and can hear them, that creature must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by the harpy until the harpy stops singing or the target can't hear them anymore.

While charmed in this way, the target can't willingly move on their turn, and they can't attack, damage, or target any unwilling harpy with any effect. If the charmed target takes damage from a source other than a harpy, they can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on a success.
A creature who succeeds on a saving throw to resist or end this effect is immune to the Alluring Song of all harpies for 1 hour.

bonusActions.name: Beckon

Each target must use their reaction, if available, to move up to their speed in a direction chosen by the harpy. If this movement would lead the target into hazardous terrain, they can make a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw before moving. On a successful save, the target's reaction is not used and they are no longer charmed by Alluring Song.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics

If forced into melee, she uses her Tentacle Hair to attack and will take the first opportunity to escape if she can.

traits.value: A creature starting its turn within 30 feet of Lenore is subjected to the following effect: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 19. *Failure:* The target gains a Contamination level. *Failure or Success*: 14 (**4d6**) Necrotic damage.

traits.name: Tendrils
traits.value: Lenore's long hair can latch onto surfaces to pull her in any direction. She has a Flying Speed of 40 feet (included in Speed) but cannot move more than 30 feet from a solid surface, including walls and ceilings.

actions.name: Lenore always takes her turn on Initiative count 20
actions.value: On her turn, she can use her movement and interaction as normal. However, she does not take an action or Bonus Action on his turn unless forced to do so by a spell or other effect. Instead, Lenore takes one of the following Epic Actions at the end of each player character's turn.

actions.name: Tentacle Hair
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +9, reach 15 ft. *Hit:* 14 (**4d4 + 4**) Piercing damage plus 21 (**6d6**) Necrotic damage.

actions.name: Contaminated Eye Blast
actions.value: *Ranged Attack Roll:* +9, range 120 ft. *Hit:* 7 (**1d6 + 4**) Force damage, plus 10 (**3d6**) Necrotic damage, and if the target is a creature it is subjected to the following effect. *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 19. *Failure:* The target gains one level of Contamination.

actions.name: Grim Reveal (1/Round)
actions.value: Lenore removes her mask, revealing her horrific form. *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 19, creatures within 60 feet of her who can see her. *Failure:* The target has the Frightened condition (save ends).

actions.name: Octarine Wall (1/Day)
actions.value: Lenore summons a shimmering wall within 120 feet of her. The wall can be up to 90 feet long, 30 feet high, and 1 inch thick. Alternatively, she can shape the wall into a sphere up to 30 feet in diameter centered on a point she can see within range. The wall has three octarine layers. When a creature attempts to reach into or pass through the wall, it does so one layer at a time through all the wall's layers. *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 19. Failure:

Layer 1: 10 (**3d6**) Necrotic damage and the target gains one level of Contamination and has the Dazed condition; Layer 2: 17 (**5d6**) Necrotic damage, and the target gains two levels of Contamination and has the Defenseless condition; Layer 3: 35 (**10d6**) Necrotic damage, and the target gains three levels of Contamination and the Helpless condition. *Success* Half damage only. The wall can be destroyed by taking at least 100 Radiant or Force damage.

actions.name: Radiant Gaze (1/Round)
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 19, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. *Failure:* 44 (**8d10**) Radiant damage and the target gains one level of Contamination. *Success* Half damage only. If Lenore sees her reflection within the Cone, she gains the Blinded and Incapacitated conditions for 1d6 hours and can't take the Epic Resistance Epic Action for the duration.

actions.name: Epic Resistance
actions.value: Lenore chooses one condition, spell, or other effect currently affecting her and rolls 1d20. On an 11 or higher, the effect ends on her. Lenore can use this Epic Action even if she would otherwise be unable to take actions, her actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters her game statistics.

fluffInfo.name: Reanimated by the Haze
fluffInfo.value: Left undisturbed in the ruins of Drakkenheim, the corpse of a humanoid character of 6th level (or Challenge Rating 6) or higher has a 10 percent chance each day of rising as a Haze Wight.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Delusional Undead
fluffInfo.value: You recognize that these creatures think they are still alive, and that we are the monsters!

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Contaminated Eldritch Power
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of the Haze Wight's Contaminated Blast.

fluffInfo.name: (20+) Awaken Minions
fluffInfo.value: You know of the creature's Animate Haze Husk Bonus Action.

fluffInfo.name: (25+) Made With Delerium
fluffInfo.value: You understand that it's possible to create these zombies with delerium and the __Animate Dead__ spell (see the Creating Haze Husks sidebar).

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Haze Wights are intelligent warriors who can engage in melee or ranged combat. However, they mistakenly believe their foes are mindless monsters not requiring careful tactics, seeing most targets as beasts to be put down. When a foe demonstrates unexpected magic or strategy, some fight more carefully, commanding minions to surround and corner their opponents.

Groups of these wights sometimes believe they are still-living, acting as if they still possess their former abilities, using teamwork and "healing" each other by reanimating the fallen as Haze Husks. Nevertheless, their delusions render them incapable of imagining defeat; they do not flee when wounded, nor when allies fall. Instead, they believe they fight in a heroic last stand, desperately rallying against the inevitable doom they already suffered.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Harpies hunt in small flocks, and always attack from the sky or an overhead vantage point using their longbows. They engage in melee only to make the killing blow on a wounded target. When confronted with a foe able to make effective ranged attacks, harpies become much more cautious. Accurate shots from the ground or an exploding airborne __Fireball__ may be enough alone to shake their resolve, causing them to fly off in search of easier prey.

fluffInfo.value: The Hazewind Harpy Valkyrie are the chosen warriors of the Crimson Countess, and they are skilled with both their weapons and their talons. They wield barbed javelins and a shield in their hands, and leave their taloned feet open to pluck people off the ground and toss them. They often attempt to lure foes into elevated positions, such as rooftops, cliffs, or balconies, and then pluck them up and toss them to their death.
If they find themselves grounded, or outnumbered they will attempt to escape and fly to the highest location nearby to guard themselves and better defend against attackers.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics

The caterpillars continue to eat and Bite a downed character even in combat if they aren't being actively attacked. While it's happy to consume living flesh, a Hazewing Caterpillar is eager to feed on delerium. Characters may be able to draw its attention or even render it docile by offering it a shard or two and making a successful DC 15 Animal Handling check.

fluffInfo.name: Roleplaying Traits
fluffInfo.value: Adventurers who interact with He Who Laughs Last must endure his mocking laughter and jeering comments, as he remarks on the futility of their actions, the dramatic irony of their mistakes, and the meaninglessness of their quests. In doing so, He Who Laughs Last carefully offers an escape or solution—if the adventurers will offer him service in exchange, one that is almost certain to have unforeseen consequences.

He Who Laughs Last loves nothing more than when mortal heroes attempt to outmaneuver him. As befitting his name, there is almost always some unfortunate upset or surprise twist the demon has in store. Even when he is seemingly defeated, he is always sure to remind his foes who will have the last laugh.

fluffInfo.name: Personality Traits
fluffInfo.value: In conversation, I cannot contain my dark mirth, which manifests from a low chuckle to a belly-bursting guffaw. Most of all, I love the moment when mortals realize the cost of their terrible mistakes and poor decisions.

fluffInfo.name: Ideal
fluffInfo.value: Mortals fear death. I play upon that fear, and with it I can catch the conscience of any soul.

fluffInfo.name: Bond
fluffInfo.value: I harvest of souls at life's curtain call, binding them to my cast of players in my Theatre of the Danse Macabre.

fluffInfo.name: Flaw
fluffInfo.value: I oft direct the play too long, delighting in extending the final act. My patience is as deep as the grave, allowing me to savor each move in the mortal game, though sometimes to the detriment of a timely demise.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe

fluffInfo.name: (20+) Powerful Demonlord.
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of his Truesight and telepathy, his Resistances and Immunities, and his Epic

fluffInfo.name: Resistance.
fluffInfo.value: You also know this eldritch entity is beyond life and death and can reform years later if killed.

fluffInfo.name: (25+) Killing Aura.
fluffInfo.value: You know of his Mortal Coil aura, and his spellcasting Epic Actions.

fluffInfo.name: (30+) Powerful Presence.
fluffInfo.value: You know his highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: He Who Laughs Last approaches battle lazily, as his mere presence causes mortals to die in short order from his Mortal Coil aura. Nevertheless, he casually ends lives using Sleep No More, Dusty Death, and Out Brief Candle, trapping another foe in a Cage of Sorrows so they must bear witness to the death around them before they expire to his Mortal Coil.

He Who Laughs Last does not fear his own destruction, confident that he will reappear if his corporeal form is destroyed. He is certain of his fate to watch the end of the universe, and even when slain his echoing laughter remains as a grim reminder of his power.

traits.name: Inscrutable
traits.value: He Who Laughs Last is immune to any effect that would sense his emotions or read his thoughts, as well as any divination spell that he refuses. Wisdom (*Insight*) checks made to ascertain the demon lord's intentions or sincerity have Disadvantage.

traits.name: Mortal Coil
traits.value: He Who Laughs Last projects a 150-foot Emanation of death and decay. A creature that ends its turn in the Emanation suffers an Exhaustion level and ages 10 (3d6) years. The creature removes an Exhaustion level gained in this way at the end of its turn, but only if it ends its turn outside the Emanation. A creature's original age can be restored with __Greater Restoration__ or similar magic.

actions.name: He Who Laughs Last always takes his turn on Initiative count 20
actions.value: On his turn, He Who Laughs Last can use his movement and interaction as normal. However, he does not take an action or Bonus Action on his turn unless forced to do so by a spell or other effect. Instead, He Who Laughs Last takes one of the following Epic Actions at the end of each player character's turn:

entries: **Scornful Whip**: *Melee Attack Roll:* +16, reach 120 ft. *Hit:* 30 (**5d8 + 8**) Force damage, and if the target is Large or smaller, it is pulled 30 feet toward He Who Laughs Last.
**Walking Shadow (1/Round)**: He Who Laughs Last moves up to half his Speed.

actions.name: Sleep No More (1/Round)
actions.value: He Who Laughs Last casts __Power Word Kill__.

actions.name: Out Brief Candle (1/Round)
actions.value: He Who Laughs Last casts __Finger of Death__ (save DC 24).

actions.name: Dusty Death (1/Round)
actions.value: He Who Laughs Last casts __Disintegrate__ (save DC 24).

actions.name: Cage of Sorrows (1/Round)
actions.value: He Who Laughs Last creates a wall of bone on a solid surface it can see within 120 feet of himself. The wall appears as a flat surface made up of one 10-foot-square panel. The wall is 1 foot thick and lasts for 1 minute or until the wall is destroyed (AC 15, 20 Hit Points, Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage, Vulnerability to Bludgeoning and Thunder damage).

If the wall cuts through a creature's space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (GM's choice) and subjected to the following effect. *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 16. *Failure:* 10 (**3d6**) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Epic Resistance
actions.value: He Who Laughs Last chooses one condition, spell, or other effect currently affecting him and rolls 1d20. On an 11+, the effect ends on him. He Who Laughs Last can use this action even if he would otherwise be unable to take actions, his actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters his game statistics.

traits.name: Stealthy Hunter

actions.value: The hound exhales flame in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw, taking 14 (**3d6 + 4**) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature who isn't a hellhound who fails the saving throw is lit on fire for 1 minute (save ends at end of turn), or until the target or another creature who can reach them uses an action to extinguish the flames. A creature who is on fire at the start of their turn takes 7 (**2d6**) fire damage. If a creature who is already on fire is set on fire again on a subsequent turn, the damage isn't cumulative, but the duration of the fire resets to 1 minute.

traits.name: Reactive Mutations
traits.value: Immediately after the ooze takes damage, it gains resistance to that damage type. The ooze can have up to two resistances from this trait. If the ooze has its maximum number of resistances, the oldest resistance is lost when a new one is gained.

traits.name: Spider Climb

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The ooze makes two Pseudopod attacks. It can replace one attack with Engulf.

actions.name: Engulf
actions.value: The ooze moves up to its speed. While doing so, it can enter Small or smaller creatures' spaces. Whenever the ooze enters a creature's space, the creature must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw.
On a successful save, the creature can choose to be pushed 5 feet back or to the side of the ooze. A creature that chooses not to be pushed suffers the consequences of a failed saving throw.

On a failed save, the ooze enters the creature's space, and the creature takes 7 (**2d6**) acid damage and is engulfed. The engulfed creature can't breathe, is restrained, and takes 14 (**4d6**) acid damage at the start of each of the ooze's turns. When the ooze moves, the engulfed creature moves with it.
An engulfed creature can try to escape by taking an action to make a DC 13 Strength check. On a success, the creature escapes and enters a space of its choice within 5 feet of the ooze.

actions.name: Pseudopod
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 3 (**1d6**) acid damage and the target suffers one of the following random effects (roll a d6):
1. The target takes 3 (**1d6**) force damage.
2. The target takes 3 (**1d6**) bludgeoning damage.
3. The target takes 3 (**1d6**) piercing damage.
4. The target takes 3 (**1d6**) slashing damage.
5. The target takes 3 (**1d6**) cold damage.
6. The target takes 3 (**1d6**) fire damage.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe
fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *Nature* or *Survival* gain Advantage on Intelligence (*Arcana*) checks to Study a Humongous Fungus Troll, learning the following information based on the result:

fluffInfo.name: (5+) From Harsh Environments
fluffInfo.value: You know the troll's Spore Slam and Grasping Tendrils Actions.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Hard to Kill
fluffInfo.value: You learn of the troll's Regeneration trait.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Special Weakness
fluffInfo.value: You have insight into the troll's Vulnerabilities.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Humongous Fungus Trolls remain motionless and observe trespassers to see if they are a threat. If combat is initiated, the Humongous Fungus Troll uses its Grasping Tendrils to pull victims towards it, then use its Entangling Mycelia to entangle as many creatures as possible within its Rotting Aura.

traits.name: False Appearance
traits.value: While the troll remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a gigantic mushroom.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.value: The troll regains 30 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns. If the troll takes Acid or Fire damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of the troll's next turn. The troll dies only if it starts its turn with 0 Hit Points and doesn't regenerate.

traits.name: Rotting Aura
traits.value: Any creature who starts its turn in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the troll takes 10 (**3d6**) Necrotic damage unless the troll has the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: On its turn, the troll can move as normal
actions.value: However, it does not take an action or Bonus Action on its turn unless forced to do so by a spell or other effect. Instead, the troll takes one of the following Epic Actions of its choice at the end of each player character's turn:

actions.name: Spore Slam
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +10, reach 10 ft. *Hit:* 33 (**6d8 + 6**) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Grasping Tendrils
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +10, reach 60 ft. *Hit:* 22 (**3d10 + 6**) Slashing damage and if the target is Huge or smaller, the troll pulls the target up to 20 feet straight towards itself.

actions.name: Entangling Mycelia (Recharge when *Bloodied*)
actions.value: *Strength Saving Throw:* DC 15, each creature of the troll's choice in a 30-foot radius centered on it. *Failure:* The target has the Restrained condition (save ends).

actions.name: Spawn Trolling (1/Round)
actions.value: The troll creates a Fungal Trolling which appears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of it. The fungal trolling acts immediately after the troll uses this action, then acts after the troll's turn on subsequent rounds.

actions.name: Epic Resistance
actions.value: The troll chooses one condition, spell, or other effect currently affecting them and rolls 1d20. On an 11+, the effect ends on it. A troll can use this action even if it would otherwise be unable to take actions, its actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters its game statistics.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe
fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *Survival* or *Nature* gain Advantage on Intelligence (*Arcana*) check to Study a Hunter Hulk, learning the following based on their result:

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Stealthy Assassin
fluffInfo.value: You know of its Invisibility trait.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Hooked Arms
fluffInfo.value: You learn of the Hulk's Lashing Tendrils attack and Reel Bonus Action.

fluffInfo.name: (20+) Strong and Tough
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of the Hulk's highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Hunter Hulks hide in the ruins of Drakkenheim, often Invisible, attempting to get the drop on their prey. Once the Hulk's target is in a prime position, it lunges out and whips its arms around them, pulling in the unfortunate target. The Hunter Hulk then devours them with its Belly Maw. If the creature breaks free, or if the Hunter Hulk is being too heavily damaged, it turns Invisible again and slinks back into the shadows. However, the Hunter Hulk will not so easily give up on its prey, and it may stalk the target and their party for a time, looking for a better moment to strike again. Sometimes it launches another ambush almost immediately, other times it will stalk them for several hours.

actions.name: Poison Spray
actions.value: One creature within 15 feet of the hyphan must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or take 6 (**1d12**) poison damage.

actions.name: Calming Spores (1/Day)
actions.value: One creature within 30 feet of the hyphan must succeed on a DC 12 Charisma saving throw or have its emotions calmed for the next minute. A willing creature can choose to fail this saving throw. The hyphan can choose to suppress any effect causing the target to be charmed or frightened. When this effect ends, any suppressed effect resumes, provided that its duration hasn't expired in the meantime. Alternatively, the hyphan can make the target indifferent about creatures of its choice that the target is hostile toward. This indifference ends if the target is attacked or harmed by a spell or if it witnesses any of its friends being harmed. When the effect ends, the creature becomes hostile again, unless the GM rules otherwise.

entries: **Quickened Spell**: When the sporeslinger casts a spell that has a casting time of 1 action, it can spend 2 sorcery points to change the casting time to 1 bonus action for this casting.

**Twinned Spell**: When the sporeslinger casts a spell that targets only one creature and doesn't have a range of self, it can spend a number of sorcery points equal to the spell's level to target a second creature in range with the same spell (1 sorcery point if the spell is a cantrip).

fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *Nature* or *Survival* gain Advantage on Intelligence (*Nature*) checks when they Study a Hypnotic Eldritch Blossom, learning the following based on their result:

fluffInfo.name: (5+) Slow Moving Plant.
fluffInfo.value: You're aware of the plants movement, Resistances, and Immunities.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Enchanted Blossoms.
fluffInfo.value: You learn of its Hypnotic Pollen action and Spell Reflection Reaction.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Tough and Unthinking.
fluffInfo.value: You recognize the blossom's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: These plants typically grow in places protected from easy access, such as a pool of contaminated water, and they weaponize their environment against threats. The blossom attempts to contaminate victims with its nectar and uses the surroundings to amplify the danger of contamination. The flower is not agile enough to escape attacks, and relies on its Hypnotic Pollen to keep itself alive. Hypnotized victims view the flower as an impossibly beautiful object and are lured into any nearby hazards.

The effect ends early if a creature takes an action to shake the target out of its stupor.
